diagnostics.message:
[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run1]
:resource.aws_iam_instance_profile.instance sets `role = local.aws_iam_role_instance_name`, which is a plain string, so Terraform does not know it must be created after :resource.aws_iam_role.instance. When `create_runner_iam_role` is true the role is created by this module, and the instance profile could be created before the role exists, causing the profile creation to fail.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run2]
:resource.aws_iam_instance_profile.instance sets `role = local.aws_iam_role_instance_name`, a plain name string, so Terraform sees no dependency on :resource.aws_iam_role.instance. When var.create_runner_iam_role is true both are created in the same apply, and IAM rejects an instance profile that references a role that does not exist yet, so the profile can be applied before the role and fail.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run3]
:resource.aws_iam_instance_profile.instance references the role only via the name string `local.aws_iam_role_instance_name` (which contains no resource reference), so Terraform may create the instance profile before :resource.aws_iam_role.instance exists, failing with a NoSuchEntity error.

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run1]
:resource.aws_launch_template.gitlab_runner_instance sets `iam_instance_profile.name = local.aws_iam_role_instance_name` (a plain string), so Terraform infers no dependency on :resource.aws_iam_instance_profile.instance. The launch template (and the ASG that consumes it) can be created before the instance profile exists, which makes launching the runner agent fail. A bare depends_on (guarded by var.create_runner_iam_role) is needed here.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run2]
:resource.aws_launch_template.gitlab_runner_instance sets iam_instance_profile.name from local.aws_iam_role_instance_name (a name string), so Terraform orders it independently of :resource.aws_iam_instance_profile.instance. EC2 validates the instance profile when the launch template is created/updated, so the profile must exist first; the two can currently be applied in the wrong order.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run3]
:resource.aws_launch_template.gitlab_runner_instance sets `iam_instance_profile.name` to the plain string `local.aws_iam_role_instance_name`, establishing no dependency on :resource.aws_iam_instance_profile.instance. On a fresh apply the ASG can launch instances before the instance profile exists, and instance launches will fail until the profile is created.

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run1]
:resource.aws_iam_role_policy.instance sets `role = local.aws_iam_role_instance_name` (a string, not an attribute reference), so Terraform may create this inline policy before :resource.aws_iam_role.instance exists, and PutRolePolicy would fail. It should depend on the role.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run2]
:resource.aws_iam_role_policy.instance (the CloudWatch logging policy) targets `role = local.aws_iam_role_instance_name`, a name string, so Terraform does not order it after :resource.aws_iam_role.instance. The inline role policy can be applied before the role exists.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run3]
:resource.aws_iam_role_policy.instance (CloudWatch logging policy) sets `role = local.aws_iam_role_instance_name`, a string with no resource reference, so when the role is created in the same apply it may be applied before :resource.aws_iam_role.instance exists.

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run1]
:resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.instance_docker_machine_policy attaches to `role = local.aws_iam_role_instance_name` by name string only; there is no dependency on :resource.aws_iam_role.instance, so the attachment can race the role's creation and fail.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run2]
:resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.instance_docker_machine_policy attaches to `role = local.aws_iam_role_instance_name` (a name string), so Terraform sees no dependency on :resource.aws_iam_role.instance even though it creates that role in the same apply; the attachment can be applied before the role exists and fail with NoSuchEntity.

----------------------------------------

Its count is tied to `var.create_runner_iam_role`, so whenever the role is created in the same apply, the attachment may be applied before :resource.aws_iam_role.instance exists and fail.

:resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.instance_session_manager_policy attaches to the runner agent role only via the name string local.aws_iam_role_instance_name; when :resource.aws_iam_role.instance is module-managed, the attachment has no ordering on the role and can fail if applied first.
